subject: science
title: Ant and Duck
objective: Classify an ant and a duck as living things and describe a basic need or body part.
introduction: Milo sees an ant carrying food and a duck swimming. What evidence shows that both are living?

vocabulary.definition: A thing that grows, uses energy, and responds to its surroundings.
A thing that does not grow, use energy, or carry out life processes.
Something a living thing must have, such as water, food, or light.

items.prompt: Milo watches an ant carry a crumb. Which example is living?
items.explanation: An ant grows, uses energy, eats, and moves, so it is living. A rock, water, and a pencil do not carry out those life processes.

items.prompt: Maxine sorts a fish, ant, chair, and duck. Which one is NOT living?
items.explanation: A chair does not grow or need food and water, so it is non-living. The fish, ant, and duck are living.

items.prompt: A class chart asks what living things need to grow. Which choice belongs?
items.explanation: Living things need resources such as food and water to grow and stay alive. A battery, shelf, or cover is not a life resource.

items.prompt: A duck spreads its wings at a pond. What do birds use to fly?
items.explanation: Birds use wings to push against air and fly. Roots, scales, and gills are different body parts with other jobs.

items.prompt: Milo watches a duck eat, grow, and swim. Which example is living?
items.explanation: A duck grows, needs food and water, and responds to its surroundings, so it is living. A chair, water, and a pencil are not.
